system_description.narrative_title: Escalating Iran–Houthi–Saudi confrontation and global spillover
system_description.narrative_summary: A rapid escalation of proxy and direct hostilities (Houthi attacks on Saudi territory, Iranian strategic moves) is colliding with hardline U.S. rhetoric and renewed diplomacy at the UN, producing widening regional tensions and measurable economic disruptions. The story is an open system of interacting concrete actors (Iran, Houthis, Saudi Arabia, the U.S., Gulf states, airlines, markets) and abstract systemic processes (escalation/retaliation cycles, blockade/bypass logistics, diplomatic opening/pressure, market contagion). Feedbacks — military strikes prompting diplomatic pressure and market shocks that in turn shape political choices — create multiple pathways for either de-escalation or rapid wider conflict.
system_description.scope: Inside: Houthi attacks and Saudi responses, Iranian operational adjustments (land routes, threats), U.S. and allied diplomatic/military signalling (including presidential threats and UN diplomacy), Gulf states' reactions, impacts on air travel, shipping chokepoints (Hormuz/Bab el-Mandeb), and regional market/financial responses.
system_description.super_system: International security order and global energy/trade system
adjacent_subsystems: Global energy markets and oil shipping
International trade and maritime chokepoints (Strait of Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb)
Domestic politics of principal states (U.S. election cycle, Saudi/Gulf politics, Iran internal politics)

variables.name: Escalation intensity
variables.description: The ongoing rate and magnitude of hostile actions and operational escalation across the conflict system.

variables.name: Reciprocal attack rate
variables.description: The frequency at which attacks prompt direct or proxy retaliatory actions by opposing parties.

variables.name: Blockade effectiveness
variables.description: The degree to which interdiction measures constrain passage of goods, people, or military assets through targeted routes.

variables.name: Bypass logistics capacity
variables.description: The available capacity and efficiency of alternative transport and supply routes that circumvent contested maritime or air corridors.

variables.name: Diplomatic engagement intensity
variables.description: The level and tempo of formal diplomacy, negotiation efforts, and mediation activity among regional and external actors.

variables.name: Hardline rhetoric level
variables.description: The prevalence and intensity of uncompromising, threatening public statements that signal intent or willingness to use force.

variables.name: Deterrence credibility
variables.description: The perceived reliability that threatened retaliatory or defensive actions will be carried out and thus deter aggression.

variables.name: Regional alliance cohesion
variables.description: The degree of alignment, coordination, and supportive action among cooperating actors within the regional security field.

variables.name: Chokepoint traffic volume
variables.description: The flow rate of commercial and military transit through strategic maritime and air chokepoints.

variables.name: Risk premia level
variables.description: The additional cost embedded in financial, insurance, and freight pricing reflecting perceived conflict and disruption risk.

variables.name: Market volatility
variables.description: The amplitude and frequency of price swings in energy, equity, and currency markets linked to the security situation.

variables.name: Civil infrastructure damage
variables.description: The cumulative scale of physical damage to civilian transport, energy, and logistics infrastructure in the region.

variables.name: Airline operational disruption
variables.description: The rate of flight cancellations, reroutings, and airspace restrictions affecting regional and international aviation.

variables.name: Trade flow loss rate
variables.description: The rate at which bilateral and transit trade volumes decline due to security-related interdiction, diversion, or insurance costs.

variables.name: Arms transfer flow
variables.description: The tempo and volume of weapons, munitions, and military-support flows into conflict-affected actors and proxies.

variables.name: Humanitarian crisis severity
variables.description: The scale and intensity of civilian displacement, casualties, and unmet humanitarian needs arising from the conflict.

catalysts.title: US–Iran talks at UN General Assembly
catalysts.description: Planned or ad-hoc US–Iran contacts and meetings on the margins of UNGA that could de-escalate or recalibrate confrontation dynamics.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'US open to meeting Iran at UN', 'US and Iran hold first talks since June', 'Pezeshkian to head to New York for UN meeting'.

catalysts.title: Iran's conditional offer to reopen Strait of Hormuz
catalysts.description: Iran signals it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz if US eases military pressure and lifts blockade, potentially restoring maritime flows.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Iran ready to reopen Strait of Hormuz if US eases military pressure', 'Iran says can reopen within 7 days'.

catalysts.title: Iran activates land routes to bypass blockade
catalysts.description: Expansion and use of overland corridors to move goods and military supplies around maritime interdiction, reducing maritime chokehold leverage.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Iran activates land routes to bypass US blockade' (reported 09-21/09-22).

catalysts.title: Ongoing Houthi strikes on Saudi targets
catalysts.description: Sustained missile/drone strikes by Houthis against Saudi infrastructure (including airports and fuel depots) that drive reciprocal responses and disruption.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Houthis launch missile at Saudi capital', 'Flames, smoke seen near Riyadh airport', 'Houthis push for control of Yemen highlands'.

catalysts.title: External military support and arms to Saudi-led side
catalysts.description: Provision of military assistance, training or materiel from UK, Turkey, and other partners to Saudi Arabia that alters balance and signalling.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'UK to provide military support to Saudi Arabia', 'Turkey says it could help meet Saudi military needs'.

catalysts.title: Wider airline suspensions and flight cancellations
catalysts.description: States and carriers suspend Iranian flights and insurers raise restrictions, increasing aviation disruption and rerouting costs regionally.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Countries cancel Iran flights after US threatens to “shut down” airlines', 'All Iranian airlines to be shut down'.

catalysts.title: Gulf and regional push for diplomatic reset with Iran
catalysts.description: Gulf states and regional actors press for a reset or mediated talks with Tehran to limit spillover and restore stability.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'Gulf states urge reset with Iran', 'Pakistan urges Iran to rein in Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia'.

catalysts.title: Iran threatens to paralyse neighbouring airports
catalysts.description: Public Iranian threats to target or paralyse airports in neighbouring countries if flights are stopped, raising risk of aviation incidents or closures.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Iran threatens to paralyse airports in neighbouring countries if they stop Iranian flights'.

catalysts.title: Calls for safe passage corridors via Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb
catalysts.description: Diplomatic proposals or initiatives (Russia, Saudi, others) to guarantee safe maritime passage that could reduce disruption if implemented.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Putin and Saudi crown prince call for safe passage via Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb'.
